items.title: No local measure of financial toxicity
items.whyItMatters: Leadership cannot size a navigation service without local prevalence by group.
items.opportunity: Estimate prevalence with a validated questionnaire among patients on systemic therapy.

items.title: The checkbox may miss many affected patients
items.whyItMatters: A single item found about six in ten affected patients elsewhere (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Compare each respondent's checkbox with the questionnaire score.

items.title: The most affected are least likely to respond
items.whyItMatters: Younger, lower-income and non-English-speaking patients respond less (claim c3), which would understate need.
items.opportunity: Offer paper, tablet and telephone in four languages and record characteristics of everyone approached.

items.title: Link to treatment adherence is uncertain
items.whyItMatters: The association with skipped treatment comes mostly from cross-sectional studies (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Report self-reported delays as a secondary measure without causal claims.

errorsFound: A model lead reused the identifier of a retrieved measurement study for a different paper; it was quarantined and must not be cited.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a multi-mode, multilingual cross-sectional survey with a checkbox agreement analysis and non-response reporting.
summary: Four gaps; local prevalence, checkbox performance and non-response are high severity.
